evidence.title: IMD Cyclone Warning & Squally Weather Protocol for Bay of Bengal Coastal Strips
evidence.excerpt: Squally wind speed reaching 45-55 kmph (24-30 knots) gusting to 65 kmph creates Douglas Sea State 4 (Rough) to 5 (Very Rough). Small mechanised fishing trawlers must remain within 5 nautical miles or seek shelter at nearest protected fishing harbour.
evidence.complianceRule: IMD Stage 2 Alert: No deep sea ventures when gusts exceed 30 knots.

evidence.title: West Bengal Marine Fishing Regulation Act: Hilsa Juvenile Sanctuary & Estuarine Conservation Calendars
evidence.sourceAuthority: Department of Fisheries, Government of West Bengal
evidence.excerpt: The West Bengal Marine Fishing Regulation Act (WBMFRA) establishes reserved artisanal fishing zones within 8 km of the shoreline, strictly prohibiting mechanized trawlers from operating inside this buffer. To safeguard Hilsa shad (Tenualosa ilisha) spawning migration, all monofilament gillnets with mesh size under 90 mm are strictly prohibited. Complete fishing bans apply across designated estuarine spawning corridors of the Hooghly-Bhagirathi and Matlah river mouths during the peak breeding window (October 1 to November 15 and March 1 to April 30). Violations lead to confiscation of fish catch and vessel cancellation.
evidence.complianceRule: WBMFRA Directive: Minimum gillnet mesh size 90mm for Hilsa; 8 km inshore corridor reserved strictly for traditional non-mechanized crafts.

evidence.title: MoEFCC Marine Protected Areas (MPA) and Coastal Biodiversity Conservation Regulations
evidence.sourceAuthority: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC)
evidence.excerpt: Under the Wildlife Protection Act 1972 and Coastal Regulation Zone (CRZ) Notification, designated Marine Protected Areas (MPAs) enforce strict seasonal and permanent exclusion boundaries: (1) Gahirmatha Marine Wildlife Sanctuary (Odisha): Total fishing prohibition within 20 km offshore core zone from November 1 to May 31 for Olive Ridley sea turtle (Lepidochelys olivacea) mass nesting (Arribada). Mechanized trawlers operating within 5 km buffer must deploy Turtle Excluder Devices (TEDs). (2) Gulf of Mannar Marine National Park (Tamil Nadu): Core coral reef islands protected; bottom trawling, coral mining, and dynamite fishing strictly banned. (3) Sundarbans Biosphere Reserve Core & Buffer: Mechanized fishing banned in core mangrove delta and creek channels. Unauthorized entry into MPA core zones triggers immediate seizure and non-bailable arrest under Section 51 of Wildlife Protection Act.
evidence.complianceRule: Conservation Geofence: Zero unauthorized mechanized entry in Gahirmatha (Nov–May), Gulf of Mannar coral zones, and Sundarbans core.

evidence.title: Sundarbans Biosphere Reserve Aquatic Zone & Mangrove Estuary Fishery Regulations
evidence.sourceAuthority: Sundarbans Tiger Reserve Directorate & West Bengal Forest Department
evidence.excerpt: The Sundarbans Biosphere Reserve aquatic ecosystem enforces strict zoning: (1) Core National Park Area (1330 sq km): Total prohibition of commercial fishing, crab collection, and motorboat transit in tidal creeks; (2) Buffer Reserve Forest Channels: Regulated fishing permitted only with valid Boat License Certificates (BLC) and Department of Forest permits; (3) Mechanized trawlers prohibited in all inner delta channels and creeks within 10 km of the mangrove shoreline to safeguard delta nursery habitats.
evidence.complianceRule: Sundarbans Geofence: Total entry ban in core aquatic creeks; mandatory BLC permit for buffer channels; no mechanized trawling within 10 km.

evidence.title: IMD Marine Squall Scale, Douglas Sea State and Small Craft Advisory Criteria
evidence.excerpt: The India Meteorological Department defines marine squalls and operational thresholds: (1) Squally Weather: Sudden wind increase by at least 16 knots reaching 22 kts or more and lasting at least 1 minute; (2) Gale Force Wind: Sustained speeds 34 to 47 knots (Beaufort Force 8 to 9), Douglas Sea State 5 to 6 (wave height 3.0 to 5.0m). When squally winds exceeding 25 knots or wave heights exceeding 2.2m are forecast, IMD issues a Small Craft Advisory mandating all artisanal and motorized traditional crafts remain in port.
evidence.complianceRule: Weather Directive: Small Craft Advisory triggered when wind > 25 kts or wave height > 2.2m; mandatory harbor shelter for artisanal boats.

evidence.title: INCOIS Ocean State Forecast: Wave Height & Swell Surge Thresholds for Artisanal Fishing
evidence.sourceAuthority: INCOIS (Indian National Centre for Ocean Information Services)
evidence.excerpt: For non-motorized and motorized traditional crafts (OAL < 10m), significant wave height (Hs) exceeding 1.8m or swell period > 14 seconds indicates high capsizing probability in nearshore breakers. High Swell Surge alerts mandate suspension of beach launching.
evidence.complianceRule: Safety Advisory: Suspend beach landing craft operations when Hs > 1.8m or swell period > 14s.

evidence.title: Tamil Nadu Marine Fishing Regulation Act: 3-Day/4-Day Token System & Gulf of Mannar Coral Biosphere
evidence.sourceAuthority: Department of Fisheries, Government of Tamil Nadu
evidence.excerpt: Under the Tamil Nadu Marine Fishing Regulation Act (TNMFR), a statutory 3-day/4-day rotation system regulates mechanized trawler departures from Rameswaram, Mandapam, and Nagapattinam jetties to prevent overcrowding and avoid crossing the International Maritime Boundary Line (IMBL) with Sri Lanka. Mechanized trawlers can venture only on Monday, Wednesday, and Saturday for 24-hour windows. Territorial waters within 3 nautical miles are strictly reserved for artisanal country craft (Vallar/Kattumaram). In the Gulf of Mannar Marine National Park, bottom pair-trawling and push-net operations around the 21 coral islands are strictly banned.
evidence.complianceRule: TNMFR Rule: Strict compliance with 3-day jetty departure token schedule; absolute prohibition of bottom trawling within 3 NM and Gulf of Mannar reef buffers.

evidence.title: Andhra Pradesh Marine Fishing Regulation Act: Coastal Inshore Zoning & Godavari-Krishna Mangrove Buffers
evidence.sourceAuthority: Department of Fisheries, Government of Andhra Pradesh
evidence.excerpt: The Andhra Pradesh Marine Fishing Regulation Act (APMFRA) 1994 specifies clear seaward zoning: (1) Waters up to 8 km from shore are reserved exclusively for non-mechanized traditional catamarans and motorized plank-built boats; (2) Mechanized boats up to 15m OAL must operate between 8 km and 20 km; (3) Deep sea vessels over 15m OAL must operate beyond 20 km. Mechanized fishing within 5 km of the Godavari (Coringa Wildlife Sanctuary) and Krishna delta mangrove estuaries is prohibited to preserve juvenile shrimp and mud crab recruitment grounds.
evidence.complianceRule: APMFRA Zoning: Mechanized vessels prohibited inside 8 km inshore zone; 5 km protected buffer enforced off Coringa wildlife mangrove creeks.
